principles: Minimal blast radius: fix the one mis-wired argument; do not refactor adjacent gates or the managed-asset path.
Symmetry with the established pattern: docs-drift should receive gitCwd exactly as channel/concept/english gates already do.
Prove the fix mechanically: a regression red against pre-fix wiring and green after, plus a guard that catches the defect class on recurrence.
Byte-identical plain-repo behavior: when projectRoot==gitCwd the change is a no-op.
Respect deferral: do not touch the english-gate storyDir mismatch (#3) or the express docstring (#2).
drivers: Wrapper-root layouts (metadataRoot != gitRoot) false-block REVIEW->TEST today.
The existing bare-identifier git-cwd contract guard cannot see metadataRoot forwarded under a param name (repoRoot), so the class can silently recur.
High priority + gate riskSignal demand a tight, well-tested, auditable diff.

options.name: A-rewire-plus-regression-plus-guard
pros: Smallest correct diff for CHK-001 (one argument)
Regression exercises the real wiring (resolveGitCwd + runDocsDriftGate + scanPathDrift) under a true metadataRoot!=gitRoot fixture, so it actually catches the wiring bug
Guard is mechanical and targeted at the exact recurrence vector
cons: Wrapper-root fixture needs a real git subdir (or faithfully injected per-root fs/git) to be faithful
Guard is review-preflight-specific rather than a fully general lexical rule

options.name: B-general-lexical-guard-rewrite
pros: Would catch the class repo-wide, not just review-preflight
cons: Param-name aliasing of metadataRoot is not lexically decidable without dataflow analysis -> high false-positive/false-negative risk
Much larger, riskier guard change; over-engineering vs the confirmed single defect site
Slower to land, against minimal-blast-radius principle

options.name: C-fix-only-no-tests
cons: No mechanical proof of fix and no recurrence guard -> defect class returns silently

rationale: Option A delivers the smallest correct fix (CHK-001), a regression that genuinely exercises metadataRoot!=gitRoot through the real wiring so it is red pre-fix and green post-fix (CHK-002), and a tight review-preflight-specific guard that catches the exact recurrence vector (param-named forward of metadataRoot to a git-invoking gate) without the undecidable general dataflow analysis Option B requires. B is over-engineering with high false-positive risk; C fails the story scope and leaves no mechanical proof or guard.

preMortem.scenario: Wrapper-root regression passes both pre- and post-fix (does not actually distinguish gitRoot vs metadataRoot)
preMortem.trigger: Fixture accidentally puts the referenced path under BOTH metadataRoot and gitRoot, or grep/exists is stubbed in a way that ignores the root
preMortem.consequence: False green: the regression provides no protection and the bug could ship unfixed
preMortem.mitigation: Require the implementer to demonstrate RED against pre-fix wiring (temporarily revert repoRoot to deps.projectRoot, run the smoke, capture FAIL) before claiming done; the referenced path must exist ONLY under gitRoot, and fs/git must be scoped by the actual repoRoot argument.

preMortem.scenario: The one-line fix breaks plain-repo behavior
preMortem.trigger: On plain repos resolveGitCwd returns something other than projectRoot and the change alters the passed root
preMortem.consequence: Plain-repo docs-drift gate changes behavior / regresses existing docs-drift-path-drift-smoke
preMortem.mitigation: Confirm resolveGitCwd falls back to projectRoot on plain repos (projectRoot==gitCwd), run the existing docs-drift-path-drift-smoke unchanged, assert byte-identical plain-repo output; keep the diff to the single repoRoot argument.

preMortem.scenario: Scope creep into the english-gate storyDir mismatch or managedAssetDefs root
preMortem.trigger: Implementer notices the english gate / managed-asset path also uses metadataRoot and decides to fix them too
preMortem.consequence: Touches deferred finding #3 / out-of-scope code, violating the user-confirmed boundary and inflating review surface
preMortem.mitigation: execution-boundary allowedPaths + explicit OUT-OF-SCOPE instruction in every implementer prompt; CHK-001 changes ONLY the docs-drift repoRoot argument; reviewer verifies the diff contains no english-gate storyDir or managedAssetDefs change.

preMortem.scenario: New smoke not actually run by the battery the user runs
preMortem.trigger: Smoke added as a file but not wired into root npm test / lattice validate (only auto-discovered by test:all)
preMortem.consequence: Regression exists but never runs in the gate that matters; silent rot
preMortem.mitigation: Wire the new smoke explicitly into the root npm test script and verify lattice validate --story=B-f882 executes it (grep the run output for the smoke name).

preMortem.scenario: Strengthened guard is too broad and flags legitimate non-git uses of deps.projectRoot
preMortem.trigger: Guard matches any deps.projectRoot usage rather than only repo-cwd forwards to git-invoking gates
preMortem.consequence: False positives break unrelated code and annoy future authors -> guard gets disabled
preMortem.mitigation: Scope the guard to review-preflight git-invoking gate calls only (assert the repo-cwd-taking gate calls receive the resolved gitCwd), with a self-test and a documented coverage note of what it does and does not cover.
